QUOTE: Struct fields are declared as `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(foo)`, so by default a field `foo` is actually named `private_foo`. Code outside the library that writes `ctx->foo` fails to compile... It is a compile-time guard, not an access-control mechanism.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the guard works at compile time by renaming the member to `private_foo`, and that it is not an access-control mechanism. It never says the layout is hidden, so the fields stay visible and sized, but the name-mangling mechanism is stated.
